Directories independent of environments. Native uses host paths; Userspace Linux/supported AVF use /mnt/term-shares/<name>. Applies to new local sessions or next VM boot.
Connections do not isolate access. Native and Userspace Linux share an Android UID.

AVF sharing on Android 17 requires all-files access. Saving copies this folder into TERM on primary shared storage; all connected environments then use that copy. File managers and other apps with storage access can see it. First close all sessions, VMs using this folder, and file operations. The private original is retained. Links and special files cannot be converted. Limited to 2 GiB and 100,000 entries. Connecting a folder does not also give the VM access to all primary storage.

This folder is stored in TERM on primary shared storage. All connected environments use the same data. File managers and other apps with storage access can see it. Revoking all-files access stops AVF VMs sharing this storage. Disconnecting a folder does not move its data back into private storage.
The shared directory was deleted or does not exist.
Saved connections apply to new local sessions or next AVF VM boot. Running sessions keep running.
Use 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, underscores or hyphens, starting with a letter.
Delete shared-directory files independently of environments and workspaces. Finish all sessions and file operations first.
Copy files separately from direct sharing. Needs a running VM and file-transfer support, including on older images.
Direct sharing needs a supported image/device and applies at next VM boot. Stop/start the VM after renaming or disconnecting. Use file copies with older unsupported images.

VM path: /home/droid/term-transfers/directory-name/relative-path. One regular file, up to 64 MiB/2 minutes. No directories, links, path escapes or overwrites; SHA-256 checked before applying.
